newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 22.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page:

WASHINGTON - The Army's civilian leader has ordered a wide-ranging investigation into the chain of command's responsibility in the sexual abuse scandal at Maryland's Aberdeen Proving Ground and into the management of the headquarters for all the Army's training centers.
SANTA MONICA, Calif. - After more than two years, O.J. Simpson testifies under oath about the murder of his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman.
WILMINGTON, Del. - A college freshman dubbed the "boy fugitive" for remaining at large after being charged with killing the newborn son he had helped deliver, has surrendered to authorities.

WASHINGTON - Last month, K&L International gave $150,000 to the Democratic National Committee, but although it was one of the largest donations received all year and the company had never contributed before, it raised few questions.

WASHINGTON - President Richard Nixon ordered a break-in and theft at the Brookings Institution in June 1971 so he could learn what information the public policy centre had collected from the Vietnam war, according to newly released White House tapes.
WASHINGTON - Lockheed Martin Corp., the world's largest defense company, has agreed to pay more than $13 million to settle one of the nation's largest age discrimination lawsuits.
